description.value: The study examined neural correlates of social inclusion in females with borderline personality disorder, major depressive disorder, and healthy controls using the fMRI Cyberball paradigm, and tested associations between neural activation and psychopathological features.

design.value: A between-group fMRI study using a 3 × 3 ANOVA with group (HC, BPD, MD) and condition (passive watching, inclusion, exclusion), followed by post-hoc group comparisons and correlations within the BPD group.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID-I and -II)

description.value: Clinical diagnoses of MD and BPD were verified using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV.
BPD symptom severity was assessed by the Borderline Symptom List; total scores divided by the number of items served for further analyses.
Current depressive symptoms were assessed using the Beck Depression Inventory, second edition, in its German version.
A 30-item self-report questionnaire rated on a 4-point Likert scale was used to assess impulsivity as a personality trait.
Rejection sensitivity was assessed as a cognitive-affective processing disposition involving anxious expectation, ready perception, and overreaction to rejection cues.
An eight-question scale rated on a 5-point Likert scale was used to examine general sensitivity for social exclusion.
The 20-item Need-Threat-Scale assessed distress after social exclusion, with subscales concerning belonging, self-esteem, meaningful existence, and control.

name.value: feelings after fMRI visual rating scale

description.value: Subjective emotional experience was assessed after the fMRI-Cyberball paradigm for angry, sad, happy, afraid, frustrated, satisfied, helpless, and inner tension feelings on a scale from 1 (very low) to 4 (very strong).

source_definition.value: Data from the BPD- and HC-group occurred at a different scanner than for the MD-group.
Patients within the MD-group were significant older than BPD-patients and HC.

task_description.value: Participants took part in a virtual ball-tossing game with two other players supposedly in another room; in fact, they played against a computer and all actions were pre-programmed.

instructions.value: During passive watching, participants were asked just to watch the game and the computer controlled their character.

stimuli.value: Participants were represented by a hand at the bottom part of a screen, while the other players were represented by animated comic figures.

task_description.value: Anatomical high-resolution T1-weighted images were acquired for coregistration and normalization into standardized stereotactic space.

description.value: T2*-sensitive gradient echo sequence; flip angle 90°, field of view 230 mm, slice thickness 2.5 mm with an interslice gap of 0.5 mm, 35 transversal slices, image size 64 × 64 pixels during the Cyberball task.

T2*-sensitive gradient echo sequence; flip angle 90°, field of view 230 mm, slice thickness 2.5 mm with an interslice gap of 0.5 mm, 35 transversal slices, image size 64 × 64 pixels during the Cyberball task.
Anatomical high-resolution T1-weighted images were acquired for coregistration and normalization into standardized stereotactic space.

Data from each session were pre-processed including slice-timing, realignment, and normalization into a standard template (Montreal Neurological Institute, MNI) with a spatial resolution of 2 × 2 × 2 mm3. Smoothing was applied with an 8-mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian kernel.

software.value: Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM12, Wellcome Department, London, United Kingdom)

steps.value: normalization into a standard MNI template with 2 × 2 × 2 mm3 spatial resolution
smoothing with an 8-mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian kernel

model_settings.value: Three separate blocks modeled passive watching, inclusion, and exclusion; six motion parameters were integrated into the design matrix. Beta images representing the averaged estimated magnitude of neural activation for each condition were computed for each participant.

A 3 × 3 ANOVA model with factors group (HC, BPD, MD) and condition (passive watching, inclusion, exclusion), including first-level contrasts for the three ball-tossing conditions. Scanner type and age were included as covariates in further analyses.
Correlation analyses between significant differential cluster fMRI parameter estimates and BSL- and RSQ-scores within BPD patients.
